summary: This document reclassifies several TCP extensions that never saw widespread use to Historic status. The affected RFCs are RFC 1072, RFC 1106, RFC 1110, RFC 1145, RFC 1146, RFC 1379, RFC 1644, and RFC 1693. The document itself is informational.

eli5.summary: Some old ideas for improving TCP were never really used. This moves them to the shelf marked old and unused so nobody thinks they are current.

subtitle: The paperwork that officially marks eight never-deployed TCP extension RFCs as Historic.

tldr.problem: Several proposed TCP extensions never saw widespread deployment, but the RFC database and IANA registries still showed them as live.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC Editor changed eight RFCs to Historic status, and IANA marked TCP option kinds 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 as obsolete.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1072, 1106, 1110, 1145, 1146, 1379, 1644 and 1693 are Historic. The justification itself lives in RFC 4614.

today: RFC 6247 is Informational and updates RFC 4614. The eight RFCs it lists are Historic, as the RFC Editor recorded when it was published.

sections.title: Why This Document Exists
sections.content:
TCP has a long history, and several proposed extensions never saw widespread deployment. Section 5 of the TCP roadmap, RFC 4614, already classifies these as Historic and gives the reasons. It does not, however, instruct the RFC Editor and IANA to update the RFC database and registries.

The sole purpose of RFC 6247 is to do that. For the justification, it points the reader back to Section 5 of RFC 4614.
sections.eli5: A teacher had already said these old ideas were out of date, but nobody had updated the official list. This note updates it.

sections.title: The RFCs Moved to Historic
sections.content:
The RFC Editor changed the status of these RFCs to Historic:

  • RFC 1072 on TCP extensions for long-delay paths
  • RFC 1106 and RFC 1110 on the TCP big window and Nak options
  • RFC 1145 and RFC 1146 on TCP alternate checksum options
  • RFC 1379 and RFC 1644 on T/TCP, extensions for transactions
  • RFC 1693 on an extension to TCP providing partial order service
sections.eli5: Eight old notes about TCP add-ons get a new stamp: old and not in use.

sections.title: IANA Registry Changes
sections.content: IANA marked TCP options 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 as obsolete in the TCP Option Kind Numbers registry. These options were documented in RFC 1072, RFC 1146, RFC 1644 and RFC 1693. The registry entries refer to RFC 6247.
sections.eli5: The official list of numbered TCP add-ons now marks those slots as old.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The only point made is a carry-over from RFC 4614: the TCP Extensions for Transactions (T/TCP, in RFC 1379 and RFC 1644) are reported to have security issues, citing a 1999 paper by de Vivo and co-authors.
sections.eli5: One of the retired ideas, T/TCP, was reported to have safety problems.
